changes: p1 affiliation changed from the invented form 'vedagarbhatarkācāryānvavāyikula' to a plain description of the lineage
p2 (Vedagarbha) confidence lowered to medium because the passage naming him ('ācāryān navāpi kula-') is corrupt
Notes now say the Śaka 1468 date is when the text was composed, not when this copy was made, and flag the unclear 'dharmmadravīti re' and 'bhuvana'

notes: This is the author's colophon, not a scribal one. The date, Śaka 1468 (about 1546 CE), is when Ramānātha composed the text; this manuscript is not dated, and no scribe or owner is named. The year comes from the chronogram read right to left: vasu = 8, rasa = 6, bhuvana = 14, giving 1468. If bhuvana is taken as 3, the year would be 368, which is not plausible. 'navāpi kulaprasūta' is probably a corruption of 'anvavāya/anvaye kulaprasūta', meaning 'born in the family line of Vedagarbha Tarkācārya'. That makes Vedagarbha an ancestor, though the exact relation is unclear. The phrase 'dharmmadravīti re' is corrupt; it may hide a name or epithet, but it cannot be read with confidence. The verse after it is also corrupt.
